name: Don Caballero
label: Touch and Go
lede: Don Caballero named itself after an SCTV mob boss, built its sound around a drummer called the Octopus, and went through bassists and club walls until its American Don line-up ended in a snowbank on I-75. The man at the kit, Damon Che, kept the name going anyway.

eras.title: A mob boss from SCTV lends a name
eras.text: Three Pittsburgh musicians started jamming in 1991 meaning to find a singer, got paid gigs before they found one, and never looked again. Ian Williams made it two guitars, and Steve Albini recorded the first album.

years.h: Three Pittsburgh musicians name a band after an SCTV mob boss
years.p: Drummer Damon Che, guitarist Mike Banfield and bassist Pat Morris start an instrumental trio, borrowing the name of Guy Caballero, Joe Flaherty's character in Godfather parody sketches on SCTV, who is billed there as "Don Caballero".
years.xp: They meant to add a vocalist, but early rehearsals turned into paying gigs, so they stayed instrumental.

years.h: Ian Williams makes it two guitars
years.p: [[Ian Williams|6f638f18-7563-4d1f-bc71-b1e2bcad3eff]] joins on guitar. The first 7-inches come out that year: the Lucky Father Brown EP on Pop Bus and "Unresolved Karma" on Broken Giraffe.
years.xp: Fecking Bahamas hears the early singles as "dark and brooding, but also deeply melodic".

years.h: For Respect puts an instrumental band on Touch and Go
years.p: [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] records the debut album for Touch and Go. Pat Morris leaves after it comes out.

eras.title: Rock, not jazz
eras.text: The bass chair kept turning over, the drums got wilder, and the second album came with a manifesto in the liner notes. Then everyone left for side projects.

years.h: Morris's bass goes to Jencik, then Reid, then Draguns
years.p: Between 1993 and 1996 the spot passes from Matt Jencik to Dave Reid to George Draguns, with Don Caballero 2 arriving in the middle of the run.

q: Don Caballero is free of solos.
years.h: The liner notes settle the jazz question
years.p: On Don Caballero 2 the band announces it is rock, not jazz. Song titles include "Please Tokio, Please This Is Tokio" and "Rollerblade Success Story".
years.xp:
The liner notes read, in full, "Don Caballero is rock not jazz. Don Caballero is free of solos."

Critic Steve Huey wrote that Damon Che's manic explosions and stop-on-a-dime time changes mapped out the path the guitarists followed. Che's flailing arms earned him the nickname the Octopus.

years.h: Everybody leaves for a side project
years.p: Damon Che plays in [[Speaking Canaries|95f2fde0-0952-4935-854b-ff9faac72f96]] with Karl Hendricks, and Williams forms Storm & Stress with Eric Emm and Kevin Shea. A free live 7-inch comes with Chunklet No. 11.

eras.title: Morris returns, and the record other bands cite
eras.text: Back with original bassist Pat Morris, the band swapped distortion for tapping and space, and made the record math-rock musicians still name. Then the line-up shifted again.

years.h: After two years off, Morris is back on bass
years.p: Che, Williams and Mike Banfield reconvene with original bassist Pat Morris.

years.h: What Burns Never Returns trades distortion for tapping
years.p: Williams moves to finger-tapping and effects pedals on the third album, and a long list of musicians keep it close.
years.xp: Meshuggah's Tomas Haake and Battles' Dave Konopka call it a favorite. Marnie Stern credits a Don Cab live video for her tapping.

years.h: Eric Emm takes the bass, and Banfield quits by year's end
years.p: The Storm & Stress bassist replaces Morris, and guitarist Banfield leaves later in the year. [[Jon Fine|7af946b0-9715-41ca-a449-e1937e98e69e]] of [[Bitch Magnet|6be97715-b3fe-421b-b478-c4462ee9de15]] fills in on tour.

years.h: Touch and Go rounds up the 7-inches on one disc
years.p: Singles Breaking Up (Vol. 1) gathers the early singles, including "Andandandandandandandand" and "Our Caballero".

eras.title: The last tour, the ice, the semi
eras.text: Down to three players, Don Caballero made its best-known record with loop pedals covering for a missing guitarist. The tour behind it came apart week by week and ended in a crash on the interstate.

years.h: Two guitarists, one of them missing, and two loop pedals
years.p: Recorded at Steve Albini's Electrical Audio. Williams and Emm layer parts with Akai Headrush loop pedals to cover for Banfield's absence.
years.xp: Nine songs, with titles like "A Lot of People Tell Me I Have a Fake British Accent". Fecking Bahamas describes "guitar-tapped melodies stacked atop each other with a looping pedal", phrases that drift in and out of time with Che's drums.
play: You Drink a Lot of Coffee for a Teenager

years.cap: Damon Che with the American Don line-up, 1999
years.h: Atlanta's Eyedrum bills Che $50 a hole
years.p: Frustrated on the fall 2000 tour, Che punches four holes in the club's walls. Tourmate Fred Weaver wrote that the venue charged $50 for each.
years.xp:
In Boston, Che refused to play his solo set unless the opening band, Pizza, came off the bill. It did, and Pizza's fans threw slices and chanted for the band all night.

The tour opened in Louisville with Che getting shocked by a microphone and walking off after less than ten minutes.

years.big: "I can't see doing another tour with Ian."
q: I can't see doing another tour with Ian.
years.h: Che throws a cassette across a gas station lot
years.p: Near New York, Williams takes Che's front seat while Che is fixing a tape. Che flings the cassette across the lot and says he's done touring with Williams.
years.xp: Tension had built all tour: Williams said the members' solo sets were ruining the band's reputation and the new record, and Che said he couldn't keep touring with him. The band agreed to split after the last date.

years.h: The van ends up in a gully on I-75
years.p: Driving to the Detroit finale in a whiteout, the van clips a slow Buick, is hit by an 18-wheeler and a jackknifed trailer, and finishes in a gully under an overpass. Everyone survives; the Detroit show never happens.
years.xp:
Fred Weaver, driving, said the van's whole left side was crushed. He wrote it up as 'The Dark Final Days of Don Caballero' for Chunklet.

The clip is the Philadelphia show from four days earlier, per its title.

eras.title: Che keeps the name
eras.text: Williams went on to Battles; Che rebuilt the band around Pittsburgh's Creta Bourzia. Two Relapse albums, a first run through the UK and Japan, and a record with vocals followed before it petered out in Spain.

years.h: Williams goes to New York and starts Battles
years.p: [[Battles|8522b9b6-b295-48d7-9a10-8618fb80beb8]] forms there in 2002. Che plays with Bellini, Emm with Good Morning, Morris with The Poison Arrows.

years.cap: Don Caballero at the Grog Shop, Cleveland, November 2, 2003
years.h: Banfield and Morris pass, so Che recruits Creta Bourzia
years.p: Che re-forms the band with Jeff Ellsworth, Gene Doyle and Jason Jouver of Pittsburgh's Creta Bourzia, after the two original members he invited back say no.
years.xp: Wikipedia counts it as a whole new line-up around Che, signed to Relapse Records two years later.

years.cap: Don Caballero at the Middle East Downstairs, Cambridge, Massachusetts, July 14, 2006
years.h: The Relapse deal brings a first trip to the UK and Japan
years.p: World Class Listening Problem gets mixed reviews. Jeff Ellsworth leaves the same year.
years.xp: The band signed to Relapse Records in 2005, and the album came out the following year.

years.cap: Don Caballero at the Capitol Theatre, December 2007
years.h: Punkgasm gives the band a singer, once
years.p: Recorded at Rust Belt Recorders in Royal Oak, Michigan. Che sings on "Dirty Looks", and on the title track he plays guitar while Gene Doyle drums.

years.cap: Damon Che with Don Caballero, January 2010
years.h: Spain is the last stop, for now
years.p: The band stops after a show in Spain. In 2014 Che told Noisey it technically still existed, as a part-time band.

eras.title: Saving the tapes
eras.text: The archive came out in pieces through Joyful Noise, and Che started a race against time: master tapes going sticky after thirty years in his care.

years.h: Joyful Noise starts digging through the archive
years.p: Gang Banged with a Headache, and Live collects a 2003 recording. In 2014 the label adds two archival sets of the 1991-92 band.
years.xp: The 1991 recordings came out in 2014 as Five Pairs of Crazy Pants, Wear 'Em: Early Caballero.

years.h: Che crowdfunds a rescue before the tapes shed themselves apart
years.p: He launches a GoFundMe to digitize master tapes he's kept for 30 years before sticky-shed syndrome ruins them, and starts a YouTube channel of drum covers of the catalog. The campaign hits its goal.

years.h: Che and El Ten Eleven's Kristian Dunn become Yesness
years.p: Che teams with [[El Ten Eleven|6c99afec-a207-4519-9d39-616880b6177b]] bassist Dunn; See You at the Solipsist Convention comes out on Joyful Noise.
